title: Hosted SSE: atomic chunk commit protocol and client-side healing for partial snapshots
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Customers observed truncated or semi-duplicated final tokens after client-visible SSE disconnects. Root cause appears to be non-atomic emission of 'chunk commit' events from edge workers while KV cache invalidation and in-flight prefix flushing occur. When a disconnect/reconnect sequence happens within a short window, clients can receive overlapping partial snapshots: a stale partial followed by a healing partial which the client cannot reconcile, showing duplicate or truncated final tokens. This ticket defines an atomic chunk commit protocol, server-initiated safepoints, and a lightweight client healing handshake to guarantee determinism and avoid visible corruption without adding significant latency.
steps_to_reproduce: Start a hosted SSE session with a long generation (200+ tokens) using model gpt-xl-quant at region us-west2
Introduce an edge worker KV eviction at token 80 and simulate a transient network partition for the client for ~2s
Allow worker to reconnect and stream remaining tokens; observe client receives overlapping fragments and truncated final token in ~2% of trials
Run with --disable-kv-cache to confirm reduced repro rate
root_cause: Edge worker emits incremental 'chunk' events before persisting a durable commit marker (non-atomic commit)
KV cache eviction/backpressure races with the flush path, causing mid-chunk replays from origin with different offsets
Client reconnection logic assumes strictly increasing sequence numbers but lacks robust safepoint validation for in-progress commits
proposed_solution: Introduce atomic commit token: worker buffers a chunk boundary until a durable commit (safepoint) is confirmed and then emits a single sealed event with commit marker
Server side: maintain lightweight safepoint journal per session that survives worker handoff for 30s
Client side: implement a healing handshake on reconnect which exchanges last-known commit token; server will resend only after validating the token or fast-forwarding to next safepoint
Fallback: if safepoint exchange fails, server returns a deterministic sealed snapshot rather than incremental fragments
Telemetry: add counters for commit-latency, safepoint-mismatch, and healing-handshake-success-rate
mitigation_runbook: For immediate customer escalations, flip edge feature flag 'sse_commit_buffering' -> on to enable conservative buffering
If customers report truncated final token: advise client to reconnect with header 'X-Resume-Token: <last-token-id>' to trigger server-side healing
For severe outages, perform targeted rolling restart of affected edge workers after draining active sessions
acceptance_criteria: No customer-reported truncated or duplicated final tokens in Canary cohort (1000 sessions) over 48 hours
Healing handshake succeeds >= 99.9% on simulated transient network partitions in staged env
Commit-latency increase < 6ms P95 with buffering enabled on perf benchmarks
Telemetry emits commit and healing metrics; dashboard added to Console that surfaces regressions
implementation_notes: Keep buffering at chunk-boundaries only; avoid buffering per-token to minimize latency impact
Safepoint journal entries are small (commit_token, sequence_number, timestamp) and stored in redis with 30s TTL
Workers must be able to serve safepoint lookups during handoff; ensure local cache warmup path
Add unit tests for commit marker generation, and an integration test harness that simulates eviction+reconnect scenarios
Coordinate with Dedicated/Private teams to ensure protocol compatibility when running in VPC mode
testing_plan: Unit: commit marker generation and validation logic
Integration: evict+replay harness reproducing the customer failure at scale (10k runs)
Load: ensure P95 latency under typical traffic with buffering on/off
Chaos: inject random disconnects and KV eviction during long generations in staging
rollout_plan: Stage: feature flag off by default; enable in staging and run canary suite
Canary: enable for 1% of hosted traffic (non-critical customers) for 72 hours
Gradual: 10% -> 33% -> 100% across 24-hour windows if metrics remain green
Fallback: server accepts header 'X-Prefer-Lossy: true' for customers who prefer lower latency over atomic guarantees
customer_notes: Customer A (chat-app) escalated with 7 incidents across 3 days; provided session traces and example events
We proposed immediate conservative buffering and offered temporary dedicated throughput until fix is live
Customer B (analytics) asked for timeline and preferred full atomic guarantees; assigned Solutions Eng to coordinate
